interviewQuestions.question: Why don't real caches implement true LRU exactly, and what do they do instead?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
True LRU needs the full recency ordering of every way in a set, growing as N! — an 8-way set has 40,320 orderings. Exact encoding costs more state bits than it's worth, multiplied across thousands of sets.

Hardware approximates instead: **clock** sweeps a reference bit round-robin, evicting the first way found unset; **pseudo-LRU** uses a small bit-tree tracking roughly which half was used more recently. Both land within a percent or two of true LRU's hit rate at a fraction of the cost.

**Testing:** whether you see this as a bit-cost trade-off, not an oversight.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: Why pseudo-LRU exists
